newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 28.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 28. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A violent clash between hundreds of roadside vendors and city public order officials in central Jakarta's Tanah Abang market culminated yesterday in the burning of two municipal buildings and seven cars.
- Three of 10 companies under the Strategic Industries Management Board made losses in 1995.
- Minister of Finance Mar'ie Muhammad said the government's foreign debt had fallen to $54.6 billion last November from $57.22 billion in September and $59.59 billion in 1995.
- PT Bakrie Brothers shareholders are expected to decide on Tuesday whether the firm will sell its stake in Indocopper Investama Corporation, which owns 9.36 percent of PT Freeport Indonesia.
- PT Berlian Laju Tanker shareholders approved on Monday the acquisition of a 20-percent stake in a Malaysian shipping company.
- The capital market watchdog Bapepam admitted it was still studying Indocement's plan to sell 20 percent of its stake in Indofood.
- PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa said it had no plans to sell 20 percent of its stake in PT Indofood Sukses Makmur to PT Indomulti Inti Industri.
- Indonesia needed at least 13 new pulp factories with an installed annual capacity of 500,000 tonnes each to reach a production target of 10 million tonnes in the year 2003.
- Sources said PT Zebra Nusantara planned to have a rights issue to fund the acquisition of a majority stake in PT Steady Safe.
- Sources said PT Danayasa Arthatama planned to float shares on the exchange.
- PT Telagamas Pertiwi announced a five-for-two rights issue at 1,000 rupiah a share.
- Sources said Bob Hasan was scheduled to hold talks with Bre-X and Placer Dome on the Busang gold find on Tuesday.
